articles.headline: FIFA exec on White House World Cup panel resigns to protest Infantino plan
articles.description: Senior FIFA adviser and former U.S. Soccer president Carlos Cordeiro, who represented the world soccer body on the White House Task Force for the World Cup, resigned Friday in protest at its private equity plan.

articles.headline: Gianni Infantino dealt another blow as AFC joins UEFA, Concacaf in rejecting World Cup plan
articles.description: FIFA's controversial plan to sell stakes in a World Cup company has been dealt what appears to be a fatal blow after the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) joined UEFA and Concacaf in rejecting it.

articles.headline: UEFA vows World Cup boycott as Concacaf, AFC reject FIFA private equity plan
articles.description: FIFA president Gianni Infantino's plan to sell stakes in the World Cup to a private equity group was dealt a major blow on Thursday, after Concacaf joined UEFA in rejecting the proposal.

articles.headline: FIFA defends World Cup private equity plan: 'Nobody is selling football'
articles.description: FIFA issued a statement early Friday saying that "nobody is selling football" and that it plans to continue the consultation process for the plan to sell stakes in the World Cup to private equity investors.
